title: Kernel-fit adjudicator and microwindow prefill throttler
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see tail-latency spikes on mixed workloads where short chat turns, long-context prefill requests, and cached-KV hits coexist on a single worker pool. Current continuous-batching admission uses coarse time windows that occasionally allow synchronized bursts, and the kernel selection path chooses based on static heuristics (sequence length thresholds) that don't account for batch composition or temporal contention.

Proposal: Implement a Kernel-fit Adjudicator (KFA) inside the admission control pipeline that computes a lightweight score for each incoming prefill request and assigns it to a microwindow slot with jittered offsets. The KFA score factors include: estimated decode token count, KV-cache hit probability, model variant (quantized vs fp16), required attention tiling (long vs short context), and a kernel-latency profile fingerprint derived from recent telemetry. The adjudicator exposes a per-request routing decision: fast-path kernel, high-throughput kernel, or deferred microwindow.

Complementary mechanics: Microwindow Prefill Throttler splits admission time into small, overlapping micro-windows (8–30ms) and injects randomized jitter to prevent synchronized arrivals. Within each microwindow we run a content-aware packer that groups compatible shapes (similar sequence lengths and kernel affinity) to maximize kernel utilization while bounding worst-case decode latency. The prefill scheduler and decode scheduler are decoupled into priority lanes: control-plane, interactive (low-latency), bulk (throughput), and fallback (degraded kernels).

Key engineering components to deliver: 1) Kernel-fit scoring service (stateless scorer with telemetry cache); 2) Microwindow admission coordinator inside the serving runtime; 3) Content-aware batch packer and shape coalescer; 4) Attention-tiling hint propagation (prefill tags sequence needing tiled attention kernels during decode); 5) Observability hooks and SLO dashboards for per-kernel percentiles and microwindow occupancy.

Goals: Reduce 95th and 99th percentile tail latency across mixed workloads by 25–40% while keeping 50th percentile stable and avoiding throughput regression for bulk workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel-fit scorer implemented and exposed via in-process API for admission pathway
Microwindow admission coordinator can allocate slots with jitter and enforce slot capacity per worker
Content-aware packer groups batch elements by kernel affinity and sequence-length band with measurable packing efficiency > 80% on test workloads
End-to-end integration tests show 95th percentile latency reduction >= 25% on benchmark mixed workload compared to baseline
No more than 5% throughput degradation on bulk throughput synthetic runs, validated on dedicated test pool
New metrics ingested into Console: kfa_score_distribution, microwindow_occupancy, kernel_path_switches, attention_tile_rate
notes: Telemetry prototype and spreadsheet with kernel fingerprints: /drive/redwood/runtime/kernel_fingerprints_2026-02.xlsx
Related spec: attention tiling hints (doc link above) — decouples prefill tagging from decode kernel selection
Initial kernel latency profiler is in PR #4821 — see linked_prs
We will run canary traffic on a single dedicated pool before wider rollout; see rollout plan below
work_items: WIP: microwindow coordinator skeleton and tests (backend team)
WIP: content-aware packer integration with kernel selector (runtime)
UX: Console panels for new metrics (Observability)
QA: synthetic workloads and regression tests (SRE)
Docs: rollout runbook and failure modes (Solutions Engineering)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: unit/integration tests and internal performance benchmarks
Stage 1: canary on non-production pool with 5% traffic — monitor microwindow_occupancy and kernel_path_switches
Stage 2: expand to Dedicated test pools for 24-hour soak; measure 95/99 pctl against baseline
Stage 3: incremental ramp to 25% of production traffic behind runtime-1.22 feature flag
Stage 4: full enable for runtime-1.22 if SLOs and no regressions
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: scoring misclassification routes too many requests to slower kernels -> Mitigation: conservative default to fast-path and telemetry-based decay
Risk: microwindow jitter increases queuing variability -> Mitigation: bounded jitter (max 15ms) and adaptive window sizing based on tail metrics
Risk: throughput regression for bulk batch jobs -> Mitigation: separate bulk lane that bypasses microwindowing and tuned packer thresholds
Risk: attention tiling hints incompatible with some model backends -> Mitigation: feature-flagged hint propagation and runtime fallbacks
open_questions: What is the right microwindow width for 4xA100 vs 1xA100 hardware? (benchmarks needed)
How expensive is maintaining a recent kernel fingerprint cache per-worker? memory/CPU tradeoffs
Should the KFA be in-process or a shared RPC service? (in-process gives lower latency, shared gives centralized learning)
Backpressure: how many microwindows can a tenant hoard? quota policies required
comments: 2026-03-02 — Asha Patel: Initial problem statement and proposal posted. Asked infra to run microbenchmarks for kernel fingerprints (ENG-271828 as reference).

2026-03-06 — Performance: Synthetic mix (50% short chats, 30% cached-KV prefill, 20% long-context) showed 30% improvement at 95th when microwindow width=12ms and packing threshold=0.7. Full results in Drive link.

2026-03-09 — Design review: agreed to keep fallback bulk lane to protect throughput; added attention-tiling hint to prefill response metadata. Action: runtime team to add tag propagation (ENG-421318).
2026-03-11 — Security review: low sensitivity; no secret data in scorer. Marked security_review_required=false. Documented feature-flag controls.
